opportunities.title: Coldcard, BTCPay, and Lightning All Broke in the Same Week — That's Not a Coincidence, That's Bitcoin's Attack Surface
opportunities.why_now: Three separate Bitcoin infrastructure exploits (hardware wallet, payment processor, Lightning nodes) landed within days of each other, exposing a pattern rather than isolated incidents.
opportunities.angle: Trend analysis connecting Coldcard, BTCPay, and Lightning drains as evidence of underinvested infra security across the Bitcoin stack — end with a 'what to actually check today' checklist.

opportunities.title: BTCPay's Critical Flaw Is Being Exploited Right Now — Here's What Merchants Need to Do Before Reading the Rest of the Internet
opportunities.why_now: BTCPay confirmed active exploitation, meaning this is a live-fire incident, not a disclosed-then-patched CVE writeup.
opportunities.angle: Fast-turn security alert post: what's known, what's not, immediate mitigation steps, and a jab at how long merchants took to patch similar past bugs.

opportunities.title: 5,000 Findings: What Bitcoin's Red Team Audit Actually Found (and Why Nobody's Talking About It)
opportunities.why_now: A sweeping security audit just surfaced thousands of findings across Bitcoin infrastructure, landing right after the worst hack month of the year — a rare chance to quantify the rot instead of just reacting to headlines.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive breakdown of the audit's findings by severity/category, framed as 'the vulnerabilities were already there before Coldcard confirmed it.'

opportunities.title: Bybit Got a Court Order to Trace $1.5B From Lazarus Group — the Coldcard Hackers Just Sent Theirs to a Mixer Anyway
opportunities.why_now: Two parallel stories this week show the full spectrum of stolen-funds outcomes: legal wins for the biggest hack ever, and mixers swallowing the newest one in real time.
opportunities.angle: Side-by-side 'already priced' take on why court orders rarely outrun mixers — use both stories to make the cynical point that tracing tech and legal tools are still losing the speed game.

opportunities.title: Fake CAPTCHAs Are Now a BNB Chain Malware Delivery System — Yes, Really
opportunities.why_now: A fresh malware campaign is abusing fake CAPTCHA prompts specifically routed through BNB Chain infrastructure, a novel enough vector to warrant a specific warning post.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/warning post breaking down how the fake-CAPTCHA-to-wallet-drain chain works, with a screenshot-style walkthrough of red flags to spot before clicking 'I'm not a robot.'
